page: Amazon Web Services i2.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance designed for high-capacity local storage workloads. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 122.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.62 GB per core, and includes 3200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It operates on the Xen hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across several computational and memory metrics. The instance achieves average ratings in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as in Passmark CPU and memory scores. However, single-threaded performance is a notable bottleneck, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores falling into the poor category, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression registering as weak. Memory bandwidth for large block writes is also weak at 18.74 GB/sec, though read-only cached small block bandwidth is average at 588.91 GB/sec.

Given the combination of 3200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 122.0 GB of RAM, the i2.4xlarge is suited for database operations, caching layers, and transactional workloads that require high local storage capacity. Passmark database operations score in the average tier, supporting this alignment. However, the older Intel Xeon architecture presents a tradeoff in raw computational efficiency and single-threaded execution speed compared to newer generations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high density of local NVMe storage relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for legacy storage-bound applications.
